_meta.note: Curated knowledge base grounding gap-closing suggestions. Retrieval-only (BM25) -- the LLM is never allowed to invent a resource name not present here.

skills.name: Python Programming
skills.description: Writing clean, efficient Python for data work -- not just scripts that run once.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Ship one project with proper structure: modules, type hints, tests, a requirements.txt -- not a single notebook.
skills.practice_approach: Refactor an old notebook project into a proper package with functions, docstrings, and at least basic unit tests.
resources: real-world open-source repos on GitHub to read, not just tutorials

skills.name: SQL
skills.description: Querying and reasoning about relational data -- joins, window functions, aggregation, query optimization.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Solve 15-20 window-function-heavy problems (running totals, ranking, cohort analysis), not just basic SELECTs.
skills.practice_approach: Take a public dataset, load it into Postgres/SQLite, and answer non-trivial business questions purely in SQL before touching pandas.

skills.name: Data Cleaning & Preprocessing
skills.description: Handling missing data, outliers, inconsistent categories, and messy real-world data before modeling.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Document your cleaning decisions and their impact (e.g. 'imputing vs dropping changed model AUC by X') rather than just doing it silently.
skills.practice_approach: Find a genuinely messy public dataset (government open data is usually messier than Kaggle-curated ones) and write up your decisions.
resources: data.gov.in / open government datasets for realistically messy data

skills.name: Data Visualization & Storytelling
skills.description: Choosing the right chart and narrative to make a finding land with a non-technical audience.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Take one existing analysis and rebuild the chart choices specifically for a non-technical stakeholder -- justify every choice.
skills.practice_approach: Recreate a chart from a report you find confusing, and write down what you changed and why.
resources: Storytelling with Data (concepts, not the specific book link)

skills.name: Git & Collaborative Workflow
skills.description: Branching, PRs, commit hygiene -- working the way a team actually works, not just 'git add . && git commit'.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show a repo with a real commit history (meaningful messages, feature branches, at least one PR-style review artifact), not a single squashed commit.
skills.practice_approach: Go back and re-do the git history on an old solo project as if a teammate needed to follow it.

skills.name: Statistics & Hypothesis Testing
skills.description: Designing and interpreting statistical tests correctly -- knowing when a result is actually significant and when it isn't.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Write up a mini case study where you explicitly state the null hypothesis, choose the right test, and discuss statistical power.
skills.practice_approach: Take an A/B test result you've seen reported somewhere and re-derive whether the claimed significance actually holds up.

skills.name: Classical ML (scikit-learn)
skills.description: Regression, tree ensembles, SVMs -- knowing which model fits which problem shape and why, not just calling .fit().
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Compare 3+ model families on the same problem and explain the performance differences in terms of the data, not just report a leaderboard.
skills.practice_approach: Take one dataset and deliberately show where a simple model beats a complex one, and explain why.

skills.name: Feature Engineering
skills.description: Constructing informative features from raw data -- often the highest-leverage part of a classical ML pipeline.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show a before/after: baseline model on raw features vs. after feature engineering, with the actual delta.
skills.practice_approach: Pick a Kaggle tabular competition and spend a session purely on features before touching model choice.
resources: Kaggle competition winner write-ups/kernels for feature engineering patterns

skills.name: Model Evaluation & Metrics
skills.description: Picking the right metric for the problem (not defaulting to accuracy), understanding precision/recall trade-offs, calibration.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: For any project, explicitly justify your chosen metric against the real-world cost of false positives vs false negatives.
skills.practice_approach: Take an imbalanced classification dataset and show why accuracy is misleading there, with the numbers.

skills.name: Time Series Analysis
skills.description: Forecasting and analyzing sequential data -- seasonality, trend decomposition, avoiding data leakage from the future.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Build a forecast with a proper time-based train/test split (not random shuffling) and show why that matters.
skills.practice_approach: Take any time series dataset and demonstrate the difference in reported accuracy between a random split and a proper temporal split.

skills.name: Causal Inference
skills.description: Reasoning about cause and effect from observational data -- confounders, A/B design, difference-in-differences.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Take a correlational finding and explicitly walk through what would need to be true for it to be causal.
skills.practice_approach: Find a 'X causes Y' claim in the news and write a short breakdown of the confounders that could explain it away.
resources: Causal Inference: The Mixtape (concepts, freely available online)

skills.name: Deep Learning (PyTorch/TensorFlow)
skills.description: Building and training neural networks from the ground up -- not just fine-tuning a pretrained model.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Implement one architecture (even a small CNN or MLP) from scratch in raw PyTorch, without a high-level wrapper, at least once.
skills.practice_approach: Reimplement a classic small paper result (not a huge model) to prove you understand the mechanics, not just the API.

skills.name: Natural Language Processing
skills.description: Working with text data -- tokenization, classical NLP (TF-IDF, embeddings) through modern transformer-based approaches.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show you understand the pre-LLM foundations (why TF-IDF/BM25 sometimes beats embeddings) alongside modern methods, not just 'I called an LLM API'.
skills.practice_approach: Solve one text task two ways -- classical (TF-IDF+classifier) and modern (embeddings/LLM) -- and compare honestly.

skills.name: Computer Vision
skills.description: Image classification, detection, segmentation -- CNNs and modern vision transformers.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Build an end-to-end vision pipeline including data augmentation and a real held-out test set, not just training accuracy.
skills.practice_approach: Take a small, real vision problem (not MNIST) and document your augmentation choices and their measured effect.

skills.name: LLM Prompting & Structured Output
skills.description: Getting reliable, structured behavior out of LLMs -- system prompts, few-shot examples, output schemas, guardrails against hallucination.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show a prompt that has an explicit constraint (e.g. 'never state a fact not in the provided context') and demonstrate you tested that constraint holds.
skills.practice_approach: Take any LLM feature you've built and write an adversarial test case designed to make it break its own rules -- then fix it.

skills.name: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
skills.description: Grounding LLM output in retrieved facts instead of parametric memory -- retrieval design, chunking, and generation faithfulness.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Ship a RAG project with a real evaluation harness (retrieval precision/recall, generation faithfulness) -- not just a working demo.
skills.practice_approach: Instrument retrieval metrics on a narrow, real document set before you even connect the LLM generation step.

skills.name: Vector Embeddings & Semantic Search
skills.description: Dense vector representations for semantic similarity -- embedding model choice, ANN indexes, and when embeddings beat/lose to keyword search.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Directly compare embedding-based vs. keyword-based (BM25) retrieval on the same corpus and report where each wins.
skills.practice_approach: Take a small text corpus and build both a BM25 index and an embedding index, then find 3 queries where they disagree and explain why.

skills.name: Agentic AI & Multi-step Orchestration (LangGraph)
skills.description: Building stateful, multi-step AI systems with explicit control flow -- tool use, conditional branching, self-correction loops.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Build a graph with at least one conditional edge (not just a linear chain) and explain the state that drives the branch.
skills.practice_approach: Take a linear LLM pipeline you've built and add one real decision point -- e.g. a quality-check node that routes back for a retry.

skills.name: Model Fine-tuning
skills.description: Adapting a pretrained model to a specific task or domain -- full fine-tuning vs. parameter-efficient methods (LoRA).
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show a before/after comparison on a narrow task, with the training data and eval set both clearly described.
skills.practice_approach: Fine-tune a small open model on a narrow, well-defined task where you can clearly measure improvement.

skills.name: MLOps & Model Deployment
skills.description: Taking a model from notebook to production -- serving, versioning, CI/CD for ML, reproducibility.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Deploy one model behind a real API endpoint with basic monitoring, not just a Streamlit demo.
skills.practice_approach: Take an existing notebook model and wrap it in a FastAPI service with a health check and a logging layer.

skills.name: API Development
skills.description: Building clean, documented APIs to serve models or data -- request validation, error handling, versioning.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Ship an API with input validation (e.g. Pydantic schemas) and meaningful error responses, not just a bare endpoint.
skills.practice_approach: Wrap any existing script as a proper REST API with documented request/response schemas.

skills.name: Docker & Containerization
skills.description: Packaging an application with its dependencies so it runs identically anywhere.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Ship a Dockerfile for a real project and confirm `docker build && docker run` works from a clean clone.
skills.practice_approach: Containerize your most recent project and test that it runs correctly on a machine that never had your dev environment.

skills.name: Cloud Platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure)
skills.description: Deploying and scaling workloads on managed cloud infrastructure -- compute, storage, managed ML services.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Deploy one real project on a free-tier cloud instance end-to-end and document the setup.
skills.practice_approach: Move a local project's data storage and compute to free-tier cloud equivalents and note what broke and why.
resources: AWS/GCP free-tier official documentation and tutorials

skills.name: Data Engineering & ETL Pipelines
skills.description: Building reliable pipelines to extract, transform, and load data -- scheduling, idempotency, handling failures gracefully.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Build a pipeline that can safely re-run without duplicating data (idempotent), and demonstrate that property explicitly.
skills.practice_approach: Take a one-off data script and rebuild it as a scheduled, idempotent pipeline (even a simple cron + checkpoint file counts).

skills.name: Distributed Computing (Spark)
skills.description: Processing data too large for a single machine -- partitioning, shuffles, understanding what makes distributed jobs slow.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show a case where you diagnosed and fixed a performance issue (e.g. a bad shuffle or skewed partition), not just ran a job successfully.
skills.practice_approach: Run the same aggregation on a large public dataset in pandas vs. PySpark and document where/why pandas breaks down.

skills.name: Model Monitoring & Drift Detection
skills.description: Watching a deployed model over time -- data drift, performance decay, alerting before it silently degrades.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Simulate drift on a toy deployed model (shift the input distribution over time) and show your monitoring catching it.
skills.practice_approach: Take any deployed toy model and log predictions over synthetic 'weeks' of shifting data, then plot the drift.

skills.name: A/B Testing & Experimentation
skills.description: Designing and analyzing controlled experiments to measure real product impact.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Design a full experiment plan: hypothesis, sample size calculation, guardrail metrics, not just 'run a t-test'.
skills.practice_approach: Pick a hypothetical product change and write the complete experiment design doc, including how you'd know if it failed.
resources: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (concepts, widely available)

skills.name: Recommendation Systems
skills.description: Collaborative filtering, content-based, and hybrid approaches to personalization at scale.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Compare a simple popularity baseline against your actual recommender, and report the real lift.
skills.practice_approach: Build a recommender on any public interaction dataset and show it beats 'just recommend the most popular item'.

skills.name: Business Communication & Stakeholder Translation
skills.description: Explaining technical findings and trade-offs to non-technical decision makers in terms they can act on.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Write a one-page executive summary of a technical project with zero jargon, then have a non-technical person read it back to you.
skills.practice_approach: Take your most technical project and force yourself to explain the business impact in exactly 3 sentences.
resources: no external resource needed -- practice with a genuinely non-technical reader

skills.name: Ethical AI & Fairness
skills.description: Identifying and mitigating bias in data and models -- fairness metrics, disparate impact, responsible deployment.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Audit one of your existing models for performance disparity across a sensitive subgroup and report the numbers honestly, even if they're bad.
skills.practice_approach: Take any classifier you've built and slice its performance by a demographic-adjacent feature to see if it holds up evenly.

skills.name: Reinforcement Learning
skills.description: Learning through interaction and reward -- policy/value methods, exploration-exploitation trade-offs.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Train an agent on a small, well-known environment and show the learning curve, not just a final success screenshot.
skills.practice_approach: Use a standard small environment (e.g. from Gymnasium) and document how reward shaping changed the learned behavior.

skills.name: Database Design (SQL/NoSQL)
skills.description: Structuring data storage for the access patterns that actually matter -- normalization, indexing, when to reach for NoSQL.
skills.how_to_demonstrate: Show a schema decision you made deliberately (e.g. denormalizing for read speed) and explain the trade-off you accepted.
skills.practice_approach: Design a schema for a small real app idea and write down why you chose SQL vs NoSQL for it specifically.
